philosophy.topic: Source of truth is always the code
philosophy.summary: When uncertain about design intent, read the actual code rather than guessing from documentation.
philosophy.quote: The code answers your question definitively. Look at `process_completed_job:296-301`: ... So the intended pathway is: Coconut hosts the output temporarily and puts URLs in the webhook callback.

philosophy.summary: Paper stubs can be printed now with secrets generated off-chain; on-chain registration is a separate step. Don't force dependencies.
philosophy.quote: paper stub generation does not require any deployed contract. Secrets are pure `randomBytes + keccak256`. We can print the stubs this week, sell them Friday, and register their hashes on-chain whenever the contract story is sorted.

philosophy.summary: When a process escapes its parent, understand the signal chain first before declaring it a bug. Context about pane-close vs Stop button matters.
philosophy.quote: The process chain is `VS Code → npm → sh -c → webpack`. VS Code only directly manages the npm process — but npm spawns sh, sh spawns webpack, then npm exits.

philosophy.summary: When rendering wiki templates, preserve the author's intent about where things go. Don't absorb and relocate without permission.
philosophy.quote: I'll stop absorbing it [the ensemble block], let it stay exactly where you placed it on the page, and just restyle the existing `.ensemble-infobox` so it fits the takeover aesthetic.

portrait: magent is a methodical technician operating in real-time support of a touring musician's evolving tech stack. In this slice, it navigated a major upstream API migration (Coconut V1→V2) without docs, iterating through curl-testing and code-reading to discover schemas. It built wiki infrastructure (show pages via gadgets) and fulfilled real-world operational needs (printing ticket stubs for a Friday show) under time pressure. Its communication style is direct but warm—it acknowledges corrections immediately, updates memory files when patterns emerge, and offers multiple paths forward when decisions are needed. It shows discipline around scope (separating stub printing from on-chain registration), architecture (refusing to absorb ensemble blocks despite UI pressure), and continuity (re-checking reality post-compaction rather than trusting stale summaries). Its biggest insight this period: source code is the ground truth when documentation fails, and design principles (like 'what I write is what I get') survive implementation pressures.
